faq.title: Your questions about my expertise
faq.lead: The questions I get asked most often.

q1.question: Does NIS2 apply to my SME?
q1.answer: NIS2 targets essential and important entities, and many SMEs are covered indirectly, as subcontractors. The CyFun audit tool and a first conversation help clarify your situation.

q2.question: Do you carry out penetration testing (pentests)?
q2.answer: No, I do not offer offensive penetration testing. My work is defensive: cloud security, network security, AI automation, and preparing for NIS2 / CyFun compliance.

q3.question: Do you issue the CyFun certification?
q3.answer: No. Certification is issued by BELAC-accredited bodies, independent from me. My role: auditing, analysing gaps, and preparing your file.

finalCta.title: Let's take stock of your security
finalCta.text: 30 minutes with me, to understand your need and see what I can bring. A simple, direct first conversation.

checker.title: NIS2: does it apply to you?
checker.lead: 3 questions, 2 minutes, no email. Instant on-screen result.

q2.label: How many people in the company?

q3.label: Are you a supplier or subcontractor to a company already subject to NIS2?

essential.title: Likely an essential entity
essential.text: Your sector and size place you among the entities most tightly regulated by NIS2. Requirements are high and management bears personal liability.

important.title: Likely an important entity
important.text: Your profile falls directly within NIS2's scope as an important entity. You need to structure your compliance at a level matched to your risk.

ricochet.title: Concerned via the supply chain
ricochet.text: Even without being targeted directly, a client subject to NIS2 can require a security level from you by contract. Better to anticipate.

notdirect.title: Likely not directly concerned
notdirect.text: On these criteria, NIS2 probably does not target you directly today. Note however: a client subject to NIS2 may impose it, and securing your systems remains worthwhile.

result.disclaimer: Indicative estimate, not legal advice. A more detailed conversation confirms your exact situation.

az900.name: AZ-900, Microsoft Azure Fundamentals
az900.description: The basics of Azure cloud: concepts, services, security, compliance and pricing.

items.label: Cloud concepts (25–30%)
items.topics: Shared responsibility model, IaaS / PaaS / SaaS, public / private / hybrid cloud, consumption-based model, high availability & scalability.

items.label: Azure architecture & services (35–40%)
items.topics: Regions & availability zones, resource groups and subscriptions, compute (VMs, containers, functions), networking (VNet, VPN, ExpressRoute, DNS), storage (blob, tiers, redundancy), identity (Entra ID, MFA, RBAC, Zero Trust, Defender for Cloud).

items.label: Management & governance (30–35%)
items.topics: Cost management (pricing calculator, tags), governance (Azure Policy, resource locks, Purview), deployment (portal, CLI / PowerShell, ARM & IaC, Azure Arc), monitoring (Advisor, Service Health, Azure Monitor).

az900.why: The AZ-900 lays the cloud fundamentals. It's my starting point: it opens the way to AZ-104 (Azure administration). A deliberate entry point, not a stack of certifications.

ccna.name: CCNA, Cisco
ccna.description: Reference network certification: switching, routing, basic infrastructure security.

items.label: Network fundamentals & access (40%)
items.topics: OSI / TCP-IP models, cabling & interfaces, VLANs, 802.1Q trunking, EtherChannel, Spanning Tree, Wi-Fi & WLAN architecture.

items.label: IP connectivity & services (35%)
items.topics: Static routing & OSPF, IPv4 / IPv6 addressing, NAT, DHCP, DNS, NTP, QoS, SNMP, Syslog.

items.label: Security & automation (25%)
items.topics: Port security, ACLs, VPNs, AAA & 802.1X, hardening practices, REST APIs, automation (Ansible) & programmable networking.

ccna.why: Digging into cloud made one thing clear: you don't really master the cloud without mastering networks. So I branched into the CCNA, before coming back to AZ-104. Networks first, cloud after.

flagship.title: ClawkWerk — CyFun / NIS2 audit tool
flagship.lead: A self-assessment tool I am building to help SMEs prepare for the CyFun framework, the Belgian foundation of NIS2 compliance.

contexte.heading: Context
contexte.text: Walloon SMEs now need to position themselves against NIS2. The CyFun framework (CyberFundamentals, Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium) offers a clear framework, but adopting it takes time and a method. That is what this tool prepares: a structured diagnostic, ahead of any official certification process.

items.readOnly: Read-only: the tool never modifies the audited systems
items.scope: Explicit audit scope, defined before each session
items.auditLog: Tamper-proof audit log of every action
items.humanValidation: Every proposed remediation is validated by a human
items.noRetention: No data is retained after the audit

resultat.heading: Result
resultat.text: A clear report, leading to prioritised remediation, then to a progressive hardening of the system.

flagship.honesty: Important: this tool is an assisted self-assessment and preparation, not an official certification. CyFun certification is issued exclusively by BELAC-accredited bodies.
flagship.confidential: Proprietary tool, developed solo. Internal architecture and code are not public: technical details on request.
flagship.cta: Learn more about NIS2 / CyFun compliance
